dgxSummaryNote: The epistemic distinction among these mythic narratives lies in their foundational truth claims: Al Fisaikra (QA), Bu Darya (KW), Antarah/Mu’allaqat (SA), and the Solomon/jinn aflaj & Ubar (OM) traditions are rooted in *historical-legendary* frameworks—blending oral history, genealogical memory, and semi-mythical accounts of pre-Islamic or early Islamic Arabia, where figures like Antarah or Ubar’s king are presented as quasi-historical actors within a real-world setting. In contrast, the Dilmun paradise myths (BH) operate in a *theological-cosmological* register—depicting Dilmun as an eternal, sacred realm of primordial purity and divine
